english.title: Show a dog with docked tail at a public event - Animal Welfare Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) showed a dog at an event, namely **(..SPECIFY THE EVENT..), to which members of the public were admitted on payment of a fee, the dog's tail having been wholly or partly removed
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(9) and 32(4) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(10) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that where a dog is shown only for the purpose of demonstrating its working ability, the above offence does not apply if the dog is a certified working dog.
(ii) Section 6(11) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides a defence for a person accused of the above offence to show that they reasonably believed:-
(a) that the event was not one to which members of the public were admitted on payment of an entrance fee,
(b) that the removal took place before the commencement day, or
(c) that the dog was one in relation to which subsection 6(10) applies.

other.timelimitforprosecutions: Complex see section 31 of the Act
other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

NOTE:
Section 32(5) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.
